name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS)
organization: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Government of India
description: The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) aims to provide financial assistance to startups for proof of concept, prototype development, product trials, market entry, and commercialisation. Funds are disbursed through DPIIT-recognized incubators across India. The scheme supports early-stage startups that are DPIIT-recognized and not more than 2 years old at the time of application.
eligibility_summary: Must be DPIIT-recognized startup incorporated in India. Not more than 2 years from date of incorporation. Must not have received more than ₹10 Lakhs in external monetary support. Should have a business idea with potential to generate revenue and create employment.
deadline_notes: Rolling applications — cohorts open periodically. Check official portal for current cohort deadlines.

name: BIRAC BioNEST Scheme
organization: Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), Government of India
description: BIRAC BioNEST (Bioincubators Nurturing Entrepreneurship for Scaling Technologies) supports bio-innovation and bio-entrepreneurship. The scheme funds startups in biotechnology, medtech, healthtech, agritech, and cleantech through a network of BIRAC-supported bioincubators. It provides infrastructure, mentorship, and funding to early-stage startups working in life sciences and allied sectors.
eligibility_summary: Startups/entrepreneurs working in biotech, medtech, healthtech, agritech or cleantech. Must be associated with a BIRAC-supported bioincubator. Indian entity required.
deadline_notes: Applications through associated BIRAC-supported bioincubators. Deadlines vary by incubator cohort.

name: MeitY TIDE 2.0
organization: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India
description: Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs (TIDE 2.0) is a MeitY initiative to support tech startups at early stages. It provides financial assistance up to ₹75 Lakhs along with mentoring support through MeitY-supported incubators. The scheme focuses on emerging technologies such as AI, IoT, blockchain, cybersecurity, and ICT-based solutions.
eligibility_summary: Startups must be associated with a MeitY-supported Technology Business Incubator (TBI). Indian entity. Must work in ICT/emerging tech domains. Maximum 3 years old at time of application.
deadline_notes: Applications through MeitY-supported incubators. Check MeitY website and TBI websites for current cohort timelines.

name: IIT Madras Pravartak Technologies Foundation — Startup Support
amount_display: Up to ₹1 Crore (subject to proposal evaluation)
description: IIT Madras Pravartak Technologies Foundation supports deep technology startups. The foundation provides infrastructure, mentorship, and access to grants under various government schemes. Focus areas include AI, cybersecurity, semiconductors, IoT, robotics, and related deep technologies. The foundation is a Section 8 company established to promote innovation from IIT Madras research.
eligibility_summary: Technology startups in deep-tech domains. Preference for IIT Madras alumni and research spin-offs, but open applications accepted. Indian entities. Idea to early-stage.
deadline_notes: Rolling admissions with periodic cohort cycles. Check the official website for current cohort status.

name: NSRCEL — IIM Bangalore Startup Incubation
organization: N.S. Raghavan Centre for Entrepreneurial Learning (NSRCEL), IIM Bangalore
amount_display: Incubation support, mentorship, and access to investor network (non-dilutive support varies)
description: NSRCEL at IIM Bangalore is one of India's leading startup incubators. It offers Goldman Sachs 10,000 Women program, the Women Startup Program (WSP), agri-business incubation, and general startup support. NSRCEL provides mentorship, network access, workspace, and access to investors for early-stage startups across sectors.
eligibility_summary: Early-stage startups ideally with an MVP or strong business concept. Indian entity preferred. Specific programs target women entrepreneurs and agri-business startups.
deadline_notes: Multiple cohorts annually. Check official website for current application windows.

name: Y Combinator (YC)
amount_display: $125,000 for 7% equity + $375,000 uncapped SAFE on MFN terms
description: Y Combinator is the world's most prestigious startup accelerator. YC invests $125K for 7% equity plus an additional uncapped SAFE. The 3-month batch program in San Francisco provides mentorship from experienced founders, access to YC's extensive alumni network, and introductions to top-tier investors. Companies like Airbnb, Stripe, Dropbox, and OpenAI are YC alumni.
eligibility_summary: Open globally. Startups at idea stage to early traction. Team of 1-4 founders preferred. Must be able to participate in San Francisco for the 3-month batch. Applications reviewed twice yearly (winter and summer batches).
deadline_notes: Two batches per year: Winter batch (applications ~Sep-Oct) and Summer batch (applications ~Jan-Mar). Check YC website for exact dates.

name: Techstars Accelerator Programs
amount_display: $20,000 for 6% equity + $100,000 convertible note (standard terms vary by program)
description: Techstars is a global startup accelerator with programs in 40+ cities across industries including healthcare, fintech, retail, agriculture, and sustainability. Each program offers investment, mentorship from 10,000+ mentors worldwide, and access to the Techstars network of alumni and investors. Programs run for 13 weeks and culminate in a Demo Day.
eligibility_summary: Global applications accepted. Sector and stage requirements vary by program. Most programs prefer teams with an MVP. Applications reviewed once or twice per year depending on program.
deadline_notes: Program-specific deadlines. Visit the Techstars website to find specific programs and their application timelines.

name: NSF Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) Program
amount_display: Phase I: up to $275,000 | Phase II: up to $1,000,000 | additional supplements possible
description: The NSF SBIR program supports American small businesses engaged in scientific and technological innovation. Phase I awards fund feasibility and proof of concept research. Phase II awards fund R&D to prototype. The program is highly competitive and non-dilutive — the government does not take equity. NSF-funded areas include AI, cybersecurity, biotech, environmental technologies, and advanced manufacturing.
eligibility_summary: Must be a US-based for-profit small business. Must employ principal investigator who is employed by the company. PI must have relevant research expertise. Cannot have previously received Phase II funding from the same solicitation topic.
deadline_notes: Multiple solicitation windows throughout the year. Check NSF SBIR website for current open solicitations and deadlines.

name: EIC Accelerator (European Innovation Council)
amount_display: Grant component up to €2.5M + Equity investment up to €15M
description: The EIC Accelerator supports European startups and SMEs developing breakthrough innovations with market-creating potential. It provides a blended finance model combining grants (non-repayable) with equity investment from the EIC Fund. The program focuses on deep-tech, sustainability, health, and digital technologies. Companies must demonstrate EU-based operations.
eligibility_summary: Must be an SME or startup established in an EU Member State or associated country. Must have a breakthrough technology. Company should not exceed 500 employees. Program requires submission of short application and pitch before full evaluation.
deadline_notes: Cut-off dates three times per year. Check the official EIC website for the current call and submission deadlines.

name: AWS Activate for Startups
amount_display: Up to $100,000 in AWS credits (tier dependent) + technical support credits
description: AWS Activate provides startups with free AWS credits, technical support, and training to help build and scale on AWS cloud infrastructure. The Founders tier offers up to $1,000 in credits; the Portfolio tier (for startups affiliated with recognized accelerators, VCs, or incubators) offers up to $100,000 in credits. Credits are valid for 2 years.
eligibility_summary: Open to startups globally. Portfolio tier requires affiliation with an approved AWS Activate provider (accelerator, incubator, VC). Founders tier is open to any early-stage startup not yet generating significant revenue.
required_documents: For Portfolio: approval code from provider
deadline_notes: Rolling applications. No specific deadline — apply at any time.

name: Google for Startups Accelerator
amount_display: Up to $200,000 in Google Cloud credits + equity-free program benefits
description: Google for Startups Accelerator is a 3-month equity-free program for Seed to Series A startups. Selected startups receive Google Cloud credits, mentorship from Google experts, technical project support, and access to Google's global network. Specialized tracks exist for AI-first companies, climate tech, women founders, and region-specific programs.
eligibility_summary: Seed to Series A stage. Product live in the market. Founder-led company. Must be able to dedicate significant time to the program. Specific regional and thematic cohorts have additional requirements.
deadline_notes: Multiple cohorts across different regions and themes. Check the Google for Startups website for current open applications.

name: Microsoft for Startups Founders Hub
amount_display: Up to $150,000 in Azure credits + GitHub, Microsoft 365, and other benefits
description: Microsoft for Startups Founders Hub provides startups with free Azure cloud credits, GitHub Enterprise, Microsoft 365, and other Microsoft software benefits. The program scales benefits with startup growth. Additional support includes technical advisory access and co-sell opportunities with Microsoft's sales organization. No equity is taken.
eligibility_summary: Open globally to early-stage startups. Must be building a tech product or service. Revenue under $1M or pre-revenue. Credits scale from entry level to higher tiers as startup grows.

name: Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) — Atal Incubation Centres
amount_display: Up to ₹10 Crores for incubator setup; startup support provided through incubators
description: Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) is the Government of India's flagship initiative to promote innovation and entrepreneurship. Atal Incubation Centres (AICs) are established across India to support startups from ideation to market. Startups incubated at AICs receive mentorship, infrastructure, network access, and support in accessing government grants and investor funding.
eligibility_summary: Early-stage Indian startups and entrepreneurs. Must be associated with or incubated at an AIM-supported Atal Incubation Centre. Preference for innovative solutions to social and developmental challenges.
deadline_notes: Support provided on a rolling basis through individual AICs. Contact the nearest AIC or check AIM website.

name: 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups)
amount_display: $150,000 for 6% equity (flagship program — varies by vertical/region)
description: 500 Global is a venture capital firm and accelerator with investments in 80+ countries. The flagship 4-month program provides investment, mentorship, and intensive growth support. 500 Global also runs regional programs in Southeast Asia, MENA, Latin America, and other emerging markets. Portfolio includes companies like Canva, Talkdesk, and Credit Karma.
eligibility_summary: Startups with some traction/early revenue. Strong founding team. Product in market or close to launch. Global applications accepted. Specific programs have regional requirements.
deadline_notes: Multiple batch cycles per year. Check the 500 Global website for current open applications and deadlines.

name: Villgro Innovation Foundation
description: Villgro is India's oldest and most active social enterprise incubator. It supports startups solving problems for low-income communities across healthcare, agriculture, education, clean energy, and livelihoods. Villgro provides grant funding, equity, mentorship, and access to its impact investor network. The Unconvention program is their flagship incubation track.
eligibility_summary: Social enterprises and impact startups in India. Must address a clear social/developmental problem for underserved populations. Sector focus: health, agri, clean energy, education, livelihoods. Early to seed stage.
deadline_notes: Annual Unconvention cohort with specific application windows. Check website for current timeline.
